newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian authorities ban newspaper edition.
newsitem.headline: Albanian authorities ban newspaper edition.

text.p: Authorities banned an edition of Albania's biggest circulation newspaper on Sunday, saying a report on planned demonstrations violated emergency measures imposed to quell recent unrest.
Nikolle Lesi, publisher of the independent Koha Jone (Our Time), told Reuters that police had been ordered to seize all copies of the Sunday edition of his newspaper from distributors.

An order from the Tirana defence commander faxed to Reuters by Lesi said authorities had stopped distribution of the Sunday edition because a report headlined "Tomorrow, 20 towns on the streets" violated public security.
Emergency regulations introduced after widespread unrest broke out in February in Albania ban demonstrations and public gatherings.

Lesi said the report, from the southern port city of Vlore, detailed calls by citizens' committees in the area for daily demonstrations to protest against any postponement of national elections due in June.

Vlore and other southern towns are still under the control of the so-called salvation committees following widespread unrest in February and March by Albanians angered by the loss of their savings in fraudulent pyramid schemes.
President Sali Berisha, widely blamed for the collapse of the pyramid schemes, has agreed to hold elections by June but says there cannot be a free and fair vote unless the committees are disbanded.

Lesi, whose newspaper offices were burned down during the unrest, pointed out that restrictions on the Albanian press had been lifted in April and said there was no justification for banning the Sunday edition of Koha Jone.
